question.text: Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) differs from Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) primarily in that:

answer.text: FPI involves active management participation while FDI is passive
FPI is passive investment in markets without management participation while FDI involves active management participation
FPI is only in government bonds while FDI is only in equity
FPI has no upper limits while FDI is capped at 10%

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes FDI as involving active participation in decision-making in the investee business, whereas FPI is passive investment in the markets without participation in management. The Trap: The source supports FPI investment being in equity or in bonds and being subject to upper holding limits, but it does not state the broader claim that both FDI and FPI can be in equity or debt or that both face the same regulatory limits, so that wording should not be used. Note: The active FDI vs passive FPI distinction, the equity-or-bonds nature of FPI and FPI's upper holding limits are covered on pages 95-96 of the NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst Certification Examination workbook (February 2026).
